title: AIOpsLab: A Holistic Framework to Evaluate AI Agents for Enabling Autonomous Clouds
problem: There is no standardized evaluation framework for AI agents tasked with cloud operations (AIOps), making it impossible to rigorously compare agent capabilities for real-world fault detection, localization, root-cause analysis, and mitigation.
motivation: Cloud incidents cause significant downtime and operational cost. AI agents that automate AIOps tasks are proliferating, but without a reproducible benchmark with realistic fault workloads and a principled task taxonomy, progress cannot be measured or accelerated.
method: AIOpsLab sets up a standard way for AI agents to interact with a realistic cloud system: it uses DeathStarBench, a microservice testbed that deliberately breaks services using ChaosMesh, measures what happens through Prometheus (a metrics collector), and tracks requests across services with Jaeger (distributed tracing). The system tests agents on 100 problems organized into four levels: detecting that a fault occurred, pinpointing where it happened, analyzing why it happened (root-cause analysis), and applying a fix. Faults come in two types—symptomatic ones where you can observe the problem but don't know its source, and functional ones where the root cause is specified. The best-performing agent, FLASH, achieves 59.32% accuracy on these tasks.
key_novelty: This provides the first comprehensive system for evaluating AI agents in cloud operations, combining a standardized Agent-Cloud Interface, realistic fault injection in microservices, and a four-level task taxonomy (detect, localize, analyze root cause, mitigate) spanning the full incident response workflow.
contributions: Agent-Cloud Interface (ACI) specification for standardized agent-environment interaction
4-level task taxonomy (detect/localize/RCA/mitigate) covering full incident lifecycle
Fault library with symptomatic and functional fault categories using ChaosMesh
100-problem benchmark on DeathStarBench microservice benchmark suite
Evaluation of multiple agents: FLASH (59.32%), GPT-4-W-Shell (49.15%), and others
Analysis of agent failure modes and open challenges

metrics.accuracy: FLASH: 59.32% task accuracy; GPT-4-W-Shell: 49.15% task accuracy

limitations: Benchmark limited to DeathStarBench microservice suite; may not cover all cloud architectures
Best agent (FLASH) still fails 40%+ of tasks, indicating significant headroom
Fault injection via ChaosMesh may not capture all real-world failure modes
Evaluation requires significant infrastructure to replicate
